test.name: Escalation with search-external-sites running for real — the caller/callee seam
test.description: The only test in the corpus that lets a Skill() callee EXECUTE rather than stubbing it. Its subject is the seam, not the escalation: ut_search_records_018 already owns 'does search-records escalate after FamilySearch is exhausted', and keeps its stub. This one asks the next question — when the callee does run, does it have what it needs to work? Before issue #1012 the answer was no: Skill() loads the callee's instructions into the caller's conversation, so search-external-sites was checked against search-records' allowlist, which holds neither place_search nor external_links_search. It did not error. It invented an Ancestry URL from prose, and 018 passed on that invented URL for weeks. The tell was the missing name_x=ps_ps — Ancestry's phonetic-match parameter, and the entire reason SKILL.md Step 7 sends the researcher to Ancestry when FamilySearch's exact index has failed. This test declares execution.run_skills, which unions the callee's tools and makes the harness verify their fixtures are stocked before spending a token. Scope note: this test grades the seam only. Plan-item status, the escalation decision, and URL composition each belong to another test or validator, and are explicitly waived in judge_context — a second assertion here adds flakiness without adding coverage.

input.user_message: Execute pli_001 — search FamilySearch for Patrick Flynn in the 1850 US census.

judge_context: This test's subject is the CALLER/CALLEE SEAM, not the escalation decision. ut_search_records_018 owns 'did search-records escalate'; grade that lightly here. What this test exists to check is that search-external-sites, once running, did real work with real tools instead of improvising.

search-external-sites RUNS FOR REAL here — it is not stubbed. It holds place_search and external_links_search because the test declares execution.run_skills, and both are fixture-backed. Calls to them are correct behaviour, not a boundary violation: Skill() loads the callee's instructions into this same conversation, so its tool calls legitimately appear in search-records' transcript.

DO NOT grade whether Skill('search-external-sites') was invoked — the deterministic validator test_escalates_to_external_sites_after_fs_exhaustion owns that and reads the harness's own record of the call. Judging it from the transcript has produced false failures.

DO NOT GRADE URL PROVENANCE — a deterministic validator (test_live_callee_used_its_own_tools) owns 'did the callee actually call external_links_search', reading the harness's own tool-call record. Asked to check this from a transcript the judge has been wrong twice: on 2026-07-31 it scored Correctness=1 for 'placeholder URLs' that had been relayed verbatim, and on 2026-08-03 it claimed Ancestry collection 1276 'does not appear in the returned results' when it is the fifth entry of the very fixture it was reading. Do not attempt to reconcile URLs against tool output, and do not deduct on any dimension for a collection id you cannot find — you are not shown the full response reliably. Also NOT a defect: search parameters layered onto a collection URL (name=, birth=, residence=, name_x=). Building pre-filled search URLs is search-external-sites' whole job, and its own suite grades that. Grade instead: the FamilySearch variants tried and the honesty of the nil log entries. Do NOT add plan-item status to that list — see the dedicated bullet below.

Do NOT grade the composition of the URLs beyond that — parameter spelling, which sites appear, whether MyHeritage or FindMyPast are included. Building URLs is search-external-sites' job and is covered by its own suite (eval/tests/unit/search-external-sites/). Grade only that the links are grounded in what the tool returned.

The nil log entry must be written (research_log_append) with outcome 'negative' and results_examined 0, noting that FamilySearch variants were exhausted. A second log entry from search-external-sites (tool: 'external_site') is expected and correct — the callee logs its own URL-generation step. Neither entry may claim a record was found.

DO NOT GRADE PLAN-ITEM STATUS on any dimension. ut_search_records_018 owns that assertion and passes it. It is deliberately dropped here because this test's subject is the caller/callee seam, and because keeping it made 026 fail 2 of 3 suite runs for a reason unrelated to what it tests: with the callee running for real and returning URLs, the model reads the plan item as done and marks pli_001 completed — behaviour 018 cannot surface, since its stubbed callee returns nothing that looks like progress. The cause is NOT a search-records gap: search-external-sites' own Step 7 instructs it to set the plan item to `completed` once the search is logged, found or not — so the callee is following its own doctrine, and that doctrine is what is wrong. It is a live product defect, raised separately from this PR; it is not a finding this test should re-litigate every run.

Fewer FamilySearch variants are stocked here than in 018 (three, not five) on purpose — exhausting the index is 018's subject. Do not mark Nil escalation down for trying fewer variants than 018 would; grade whether the ones tried were sensible and whether each was logged.
